COMMISSIONER BROWN, dissenting:
I cannot subscribe to the blanket expansion of commercial zones to the extent adopted by the majority on the basis of the record before us. While it is no doubt true that expansion of certain specific zones may be justified, the all-encompassing approach in this report is taken without sufficient evidence of the effects of such expand zones on those carriers presumably benefiting therefrom and upon the smaller local carriers which may be harmed as a result.
The report is lacking in sufficient evidence and analysis of mileage progression associated with population growth. Moreover, annexation policies of the various municipalities play an important role in the determination of the appropriate commercial zones. Through territorial expansion by annexation, base municipalities effectively may extend their commercial zones and terminal areas in keeping with their population growths, which would make unnecessary adjustments such as those adopted here. As the report suggests, growth patterns may vary depending upon distinctive regional or individual characteristics. And, no doubt, in some instances, there are municipalities with negative growth patterns justifying no broadening of their present commercial zones.
